name: cancerproteome

download_files.access: public (requires standard browser User-Agent header; default curl UA returns 403)
download_files.description: Mapping of cancer type abbreviation (e.g. LAML, BRCA) to uniform full name (e.g. Acute Myeloid Leukemia)
Differential canonical protein expression (control vs. tumor) per cancer type/dataset
Differential microprotein (ribo-seq-supported small ORF) expression, control vs. tumor
Differential PTM site-level expression on canonical proteins, control vs. tumor
Differential PTM site-level expression on microproteins, control vs. tumor
Protein expression vs. drug IC50 sensitivity correlations (DepMap/GDSC drugs) per cancer type

primary_key.type: custom (GeneSymbol_UniProtAccession composite, e.g. HEXB_P07686; some entries use non-canonical suffixes like '_Canonical_4' or '_pseudogene_MP_4' for isoforms/microproteins lacking a UniProt accession)

license.observed_site: no explicit license text found on live site; only copyright notice '© 2023 College of Bioinformatics Science and Technology, Harbin Medical University'
restrictions: non-commercial re-use per paper; site itself does not restate license terms — MISMATCH/gap between paper and site

paper_vs_reality.claim: 84,257 PTM sites (paper text mentions differing PTM site counts across versions)

paper_vs_reality.observed: site lists 7,406 (labeled 'normal samples' on homepage, likely a mislabeled combined total) and 21 cancer types
no license text visible on live site pages

risks: Protein identifier field is a composite string (GeneSymbol_UniProtAccession) with inconsistent suffix patterns for isoforms/microproteins (e.g. '_Canonical_4', '_pseudogene_MP_4') — will require regex-based parsing to reliably extract UniProt accessions; not all rows have a clean UniProt ID
Site returns 403 Forbidden to default/bot User-Agent strings; a plugin dumper must set a realistic browser User-Agent header to fetch files reliably

protein_inf.txt paper-vs-site protein count mismatch (31,120 vs, 35,231) suggests the site has been updated since publication without a versioned release note — recommend re-checking counts at ingestion time
No license text on the live site itself; relying solely on the paper's CC BY-NC statement for compliance

cancer field requires a manual crosswalk from TCGA-style abbreviation to MONDO/DOID for full BioThings disease-entity alignment; cancer_names.txt only provides a human-readable name, not an ontology ID
